method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's no where it says no; `not covered` with a reason where it does not answer); the dates in one module, the rules and exported questions in another, the cases in a third; two regulative rules (s 17K(3) and s 32J(5), PARTY ... MUST ... WITHIN 28 HENCE FULFILLED LEST BREACH BY ... BECAUSE), asserted through EVALTRACE; the exported questions take only plain facts; every satisfaction, finding or discretion of the court asked as an input; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Personal Injuries (Liabilities and Damages) Act 2003 (NT), Act No. 3 of 2003, reprint REPP078 as in force at 25 March 2024 (last amended by the Justice and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024), current on the NT Legislation register on 6 November 2026, as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/Personal-Injuries-Liabilities-and-Damages-Act-2003-NT-current-reprint-REPP078.txt. No regulations under the Act are deposited.

seat: the injured person who brings the claim (the claimant); for Part 3A the person abused as a child in an institution's care; for Part 4A both the person in custody who sues for assault, battery or false imprisonment, and the victim who sues that offender (pild-claimant.l4)

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run pild-dates.l4 ; l4 run pild-claimant.l4 ; l4 run pild-cases-claimant.l4
checks.result: 215 assertions written, 215 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file; 2 #TRACEs breach as their expect lines say (2026-11-07); two deliberately wrong assertions in a scratch file showed as failed
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. A residual or breached DEONTIC cannot be compared with EQUALS on this l4, so the rules are asserted through CONSIDER EVALTRACE ... WHEN FULFILLED. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: The whole operative Act, from the claimant's seat. In: s 3 (child abuse, intoxicated, as used); s 4; s 5; s 7(1)-(4), (6), (7); s 7A with s 36; s 8; s 9; s 10; ss 12, 13 (with s 35(2)); ss 14-17; Part 3A ss 17B, 17C, 17D-17G (with s 17F(5)), 17H, 17J, 17K, 17L, 17M(3), 17P, 17Q(1), 17R; Part 4 ss 18-23, 25, 27, 29-32; Part 4A ss 32A-32H, 32J(4), (5), 32K (in the victim's answer), 32M, 32P. Out: ss 1, 2, 6, 11, 24, Parts 5-7 save ss 35(2), 36 (machinery, purposes, transitional); s 7(5) (indemnity agreements between volunteer and organisation: not the claimant's matter); s 17A (definitions used in words); s 17D (stated in the s 17E/17F answers); ss 17E(3), 17F(3), 17G(2) (matters the court weighs: folded into the court's finding, an input); s 17M(1), (2), (4), s 17N (trustees' powers); s 17Q(2)-(4), s 17S (procedure and court rules); s 26 (evidence of impairment: the degree is an input); s 32J(1)-(3), (6), (7) (the public entity's notice: in the victim's answer); s 32K(3)-(6) (in the answer); s 32L, s 32N. Reasons in NOTES.md.
